Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

new paragraph the market begins friday morning and the pottery is meant for the long table beside the north windows priya said the bowls will be arranged in groups of four with the pitchers at the ends and the tile display will sit on a low board behind them she asked that noel tell her if any carton is missing before he leaves the lane because she has to report the delivery count to the organizers the old ferry building has a second loading door on quay street but that door is reserved for the food stall crew on thursday the ceramics van should use the lantern lane entrance described above and the buyer will meet the driver there after ten thirty", "output": "Tuesday morning, I spoke with Elian Park at the Willow Bend Ceramics workshop about the delivery scheduled for the Old Ferry Building in North Harbor. The order has six cartons of serving bowls, two cartons of blue glazed pitchers, and one long crate of display tiles. The workshop packed the bowls in straw-colored paper and marked each carton with a small green square. The pitchers have white labels, and the tile crate has a red label at both ends. Elian said the pottery was made for the winter market and that the delivery note should stay with the long crate because the buyer wants the clay and glaze descriptions for the table display. The van is booked for Thursday, and the driver is Noel Vance, who has used the harbor road before.

The delivery address is the side entrance on Lantern Lane, not the public entrance facing the plaza. The side entrance has a short covered ramp and a brass bell beside the door. The property manager, Lena Cho, said the bell is working, but the outer gate can stick after rain. She asked us not to leave any carton in the open courtyard because a roof drain empties there and water gathers near the stone step. Noel needs to call her from the curb before bringing the trolley up. She will unlock the gate from inside and meet him by the service door. The workshop has supplied a phone number for its packing room, but that number is not the number for the property manager.

I am forwarding the delivery note and the contact sheet to Noel this afternoon so he can check the carton count before he leaves the depot. Elian asked me to keep the buyer copied on the message because the buyer is arranging the market tables and needs to know whether the display tiles are traveling with the bowls. Elian said, “Please do not set the tile crate on its narrow side. The corners are clean, and we want them to stay that way.” The crate has two wooden runners along its base, and Noel should place both runners flat on the trolley. The delivery note lists the tile crate as one piece, even though the foam inside separates the tiles into three bundles.

The buyer is Priya Senn, and she will be at the building after ten thirty. She has reserved a space by the service entrance for the van until eleven forty-five. After that, the market organizers need the lane clear for a food stall delivery. She said, “I can help count the cartons, but I cannot move the long crate by myself.” Noel can unload the bowls and pitchers with the hand trolley, but he should ask Priya or Lena before moving the crate from the van. The trolley straps are in the side compartment, and one strap has a loose buckle that Elian has marked with yellow tape.

Now the numbered section:
1. First, confirm the nine cartons and the single crate against the delivery note before opening the rear doors.
2. Second, keep the pitchers upright because the paper dividers shift if a carton is laid flat.
3. Third, put the delivery note in the clear sleeve on the tile crate after Priya has checked the address.
4. Fourth, photograph the red labels before unloading and send the pictures to the workshop group chat.
5. Fifth, do not stack the bowls above the blue line printed on the carton sides.

These points are written on the packing sheet as well as in the message Elian asked me to forward, and Noel has a paper copy in the glove box.

There is one condition that affects the unloading plan: if the ramp is dry and the outer gate opens without force, Noel can take the trolley directly to the service door. If rain has made the ramp slick, he should wait at the curb while Lena brings out the rubber mat and confirms that the path is clear. The forecast calls for showers after noon, but it does not say whether the harbor will get rain in the morning. The workshop does not want the cartons carried through the public entrance even if the side gate is slow because that entrance opens into the market hall and the table crews will be setting up there.

Elian also mentioned that the blue pitchers came from a separate kiln batch and the glaze on two handles looks slightly darker than the rest. The buyer has seen the sample photograph and agreed to receive the batch as packed, but the delivery note does not mark those two pitchers separately. Elian wants Noel to leave the cartons closed unless the buyer asks to inspect one of them. The bowl cartons contain a small card with care instructions, and the card should remain inside the carton. The market staff may ask whether the bowls are safe for hot soup, and Priya has the workshop answer printed on a separate sheet in her folder.

I have forwarded the delivery note, contact sheet, and packing sheet to Noel's work address and copied Priya and Elian on the message. The photograph of the red labels is still attached to the original workshop email, and Noel should be able to open it on his phone. If the signal is weak inside the harbor building, he can use the paper copy of the packing sheet instead. Lena's number is listed first on the contact sheet, and the workshop packing room number is listed beneath it. The two entries have different area codes, so they should not be confused before the driver leaves the depot.

The market begins Friday morning, and the pottery is meant for the long table beside the north windows. Priya said the bowls will be arranged in groups of four, with the pitchers at the ends, and the tile display will sit on a low board behind them. She asked that Noel tell her if any carton is missing before he leaves the lane because she has to report the delivery count to the organizers. The Old Ferry Building has a second loading door on Quay Street, but that door is reserved for the food stall crew on Thursday. The ceramics van should use the Lantern Lane entrance described above, and the buyer will meet the driver there after ten thirty."}]
